title: Workshop
description: Settings for the guided workshop panel.

defaultWorkshop.title: Default workshop
defaultWorkshop.description: Directory of the workshop to open when JupyterLab starts and no workshop was open before, relative to the JupyterLab root directory. Leave empty to open nothing.

browseOnStart.title: Browse workshops on start
browseOnStart.description: Open the workshop browser in place of the launcher, with both sidebars collapsed, when JupyterLab starts with no workshop to open or restore. Used by images that offer a choice of workshops.

panelSide.title: Panel side
panelSide.description: Which sidebar the workshop panel starts in. Moving the panel by hand is remembered by JupyterLab's layout, and a workshop whose manifest sets instructions.side overrides this.

workshopsDirectory.title: Workshops directory
workshopsDirectory.description: Directory, relative to the JupyterLab root, into which downloaded workshops are placed; "." or an empty value is the root itself. When it holds a library.json registry it is a workshop library: downloads go under installed/, the owner's own workshops under personal/, projects under projects/, and the registry holds the subscriptions in place of the collections and catalogs settings.

defaultTrustLevel.title: Default trust level
defaultTrustLevel.description: Trust level selected by default in the trust dialog for workshops without a stored decision.

trustPolicy.title: Trust policy
trustPolicy.description: Administrator overrides, typically set through overrides.json.

forcedLevel.title: Forced trust level
forcedLevel.description: When set, every workshop opens at this level and the trust dialog is not shown.

trustedSources.title: Trusted sources
trustedSources.description: Source key prefixes that open as trusted without asking, such as "git:https://github.com/GrahamDumpleton/" or "local:examples/".

disabledCapabilities.title: Disabled capabilities
disabledCapabilities.description: Capabilities that never run regardless of the trust level.

disabledFeatures.title: Disabled features
disabledFeatures.description: Parts of the extension to remove for a locked-down deployment, typically set through overrides.json. Each key removes every entry point for a feature: panel buttons, browser buttons and sections, launcher cards, palette commands and launch link parameters. "open-directory" and "open-url" leave the workshops of the subscribed collections and the installed ones openable; "collections" and "catalogs" stop learners changing their subscriptions, leaving the settings to say what is subscribed to; "available" hides the Available section of the browser; "install-all" removes the Install all button and Remove all menu item of a collection, leaving single installs; "click-hint" stops the first action of a workshop being pointed out to a learner who has clicked nothing; "library" ignores a workshop library registry (library.json) in the workshops directory and never offers to make one, so the directory behaves as a plain one; "personal" hides the My workshops section of a workshop library; "ai-authoring" removes Workshop Author, the AI agent that writes and revises your own workshops, which otherwise appears only in a workshop library on a server with the ai extra installed; "journal" removes the Journal button of a workshop library, which shows the record the library keeps of what its owner has done in it; "mentor" removes the mentor, the conversation above workshops that reads the journal, keeps the owner's profile and hands over to Workshop Author, with its welcome card, button and command.

collections.title: Collections
collections.description: Subscribed collections: published lists of workshops that can be installed, as http(s) URLs of their collection.json files or paths relative to the JupyterLab root. The workshop browser offers every subscribed collection's workshops, and its Collections dialog edits this list.

catalogs.title: Catalogs
catalogs.description: Subscribed catalogs: published lists of collections, as http(s) URLs of their catalog.json files or paths relative to the JupyterLab root. The browser offers their collections to subscribe to.

welcome.title: Welcome message
welcome.description: Path, relative to the JupyterLab root, of a Markdown file shown in a dialog when JupyterLab starts, once per browser for this server; a level-one heading on its first line is the dialog's title. Typically set through overrides.json by a deployment such as a Binder repository, to say what its workshops are for and how to end the session. A welcome launch link parameter names a file to show for that session instead.

welcomeOnLaunch.title: Welcome message under a launch link
welcomeOnLaunch.description: Whether the welcome message named by the welcome setting is also shown when a launch link opens a workshop, a collection or a catalog. Off, it is shown only to someone who arrives without one, which suits a site whose message explains how to arrive with one. A welcome launch link parameter is shown either way.

analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.description: Administrator reporting of progress events, typically set through overrides.json. When a sink is set here it applies to every workshop without asking, ahead of any analytics block a subscribed collection or a workshop manifest declares; otherwise report says whether those blocks apply with the learner's opt-in, always, or never. Events are always written to _workshop/events.jsonl in the workshop directory.

sink.title: Sink URL
sink.description: URL that receives batches of events as JSON lines by POST. Leave empty to report to the sink a collection or a workshop declares, as report says.

report.title: Report
report.description: How the sink a subscribed collection or a workshop manifest declares applies when none is set here: "ask" offers it in the trust dialog and reports only when the learner opts in, "always" reports to it without asking, and "never" reports to no such sink.

token.title: Token
token.description: Token sent as a bearer credential in the Authorization header of every batch, issued by the sink's operator. Public wherever the block is public. Leave empty for a sink that needs none.

labels.title: Labels
labels.description: Key and value pairs stamped on every event so reports can slice by them: a course, a cohort, a term. Labels are for slicing, never for identity; the workshop's name, source, collection, host and frontend are fields every event already carries. At most 16 labels.

identity.title: Identity
identity.description: Whether events carry the JupyterHub user name ("hub") or no identity ("none").

ai.title: AI
ai.description: Workshop Author, the AI agent that writes and revises your own workshops in a workshop library. It appears only on a server with the ai extra installed, and uses the credentials Claude Code has where JupyterLab was started.

model.title: Model
model.description: The model a new Workshop Author conversation starts with, such as sonnet, opus or claude-sonnet-5. Leave empty for the agent's default. The panel can change it for one workshop's conversation.

effort.title: Effort
effort.description: How much effort a new Workshop Author conversation starts with, for models that take an effort level. Leave empty for the model's default. The panel can change it for one workshop's conversation.
